title: New Voya research demonstrates plans built on behavioral insights doubled savings-rate gains
summary: .q4default .bwlistdisc { list-style-type: disc }Retrospective analysis finds automatic savings features and digital engagement can help workers save more for retirement
body_markdown:
*Retrospective analysis finds automatic savings features and digital engagement can help workers save more for retirement*


WINDSOR, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Voya Financial, Inc. (NYSE: VOYA) marks the 10th anniversary of its Behavioral Finance Institute for Innovation (the Institute) with new research showing that retirement plans built around how people make financial decisions can help workers save more. The nearly decade-long analysis found participants in plans created with behavioral science to make saving easier and more automatic increased their average savings rates by 3.33 percentage points, more than double the 1.64-point increase in traditional plans without auto-enroll and auto-escalate features.


Launched in 2016, the Institute brings together behavioral science, research and technology to better understand what helps people take meaningful financial action. This work has led to Voya’s approach to automatic savings features, personalized communications, digital experiences and retirement income solutions.


“People shouldn’t have to think about retirement every day to keep making progress toward it,” said Tom Armstrong, vice president of Customer Analytics and head of Voya’s Behavioral Finance Institute for Innovation. “Between paying everyday bills and taking care of family, it’s easy for long-term goals to get pushed aside. Our focus is on making saving easier and more intuitive, so people can continue building for the future while managing the demands of today.”


Key findings from[Voya's analysis](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.voya.com%2Fvoya-insights%2Ften-years-behavioral-innovation-what-decade-data-has-taught-us-about-benefits-design%3FauHash%3D6fow-DLEQhk7KsXOh3Zm0KOS8M58ZZYJ5DjFAKhOON0&esheet=54639892&newsitemid=20261112887391&lan=en-US&anchor=Voya%27s+analysis&index=1&md5=e73b3ed43127998a06409399847d519c) include:


- **Smarter plan design was linked to more than twice the improvement in savings rates.** Participants in plans designed to make effective saving behaviors easier increased their average savings rate by 3.33 percentage points, compared with a 1.64-point increase in more traditional plans.


- **Automatic saving features made a meaningful difference.** Plans with both automatic enrollment and automatic escalation saw savings rates increase by 3.56 percentage points, more than twice the improvement in plans without those features.


- **Automation helped even when people weren’t actively engaging online.** Among participants who were not digitally engaged, savings rates increased by 4.09 percentage points in plans with automatic enrollment and escalation, compared with 0.99 points in traditional plans.


- **The combination of strong plan design and digital engagement showed particularly strong results.** Digitally engaged participants in plans designed around behavioral insights saved more than 11% of pay on average and increased their account balances by 234.4%*


“What we’ve learned over the past decade is that better outcomes often start with better design,” said Dr. Christelle Ngnoumen, lead research director for Voya’s Behavioral Finance Institute for Innovation. “When saving is easier and supported by the right digital experiences, people are better positioned to take positive steps toward retirement and their broader financial goals.”


**Turning behavioral insights into greater financial confidence**
Since 2016, the Institute’s research has demonstrated how thoughtful plan design, clear communications and useful digital tools can remove barriers and make it easier for people to make progress towards their financial goals. Together with insights from[America’s Financial Confidence Index](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.voya.com%2Ffinancial-confidence-index&esheet=54639892&newsitemid=20261112887391&lan=en-US&anchor=America%26%238217%3Bs+Financial+Confidence+Index&index=2&md5=28acde7c9bb07391e00a4184bf02a558) , these findings help inform Guided Confidence™, Voya’s approach to making it easier for people to take action toward their financial goals.


For employers and plan sponsors, the research points to a straightforward approach: create a strong savings foundation through automatic features and thoughtful defaults, build on it with personalized digital experiences and projections, and provide timely prompts that make the next step towards their goals clear and easy to take.


**Applying insights to what comes next**
As technology continues to change how people access financial information and guidance, Voya believes behavioral science will become even more important in helping ensure those experiences lead to better decisions, not simply more information.


The Institute’s next chapter will explore how behavioral science, AI-enabled digital experiences and human expertise can work together to make financial guidance more personal, timely and useful. The research will examine how technology can complement human guidance, expand opportunities for testing and learning, and create new ways to support people while keeping their individual needs and behaviors at the center.


Learn more about Voya’s Behavioral Finance Institute for Innovation and its 10-year retrospective analysis at[Voya.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.voya.com%2Fvoya-insights%2Ften-years-behavioral-innovation-what-decade-data-has-taught-us-about-benefits-design%3FauHash%3D6fow-DLEQhk7KsXOh3Zm0KOS8M58ZZYJ5DjFAKhOON0&esheet=54639892&newsitemid=20261112887391&lan=en-US&anchor=Voya.com&index=3&md5=83533d1754204ca009f8de07c93c3212) .

**Methodology**
Voya Behavioral Finance Institute, October 2026. Retrospective analysis of 310,931 retirement participants across 877 plans who were active from 2017–2026, comparing outcomes by plan design features and engagement with Voya’s digital experiences.
